attributes.probed_form: KEPT (commit ca98f65d3): eighteen declarations deleted from src/game/game/gamemain.c and their 44 reference sites rewritten to the C string literal the retail DOL holds at that address -- lbl_80346A90 "%s%d", lbl_80346A98 "%s%c", lbl_80346AA0 "L1", lbl_80346AB0 "COMPASS", lbl_80346AC0 "%s", lbl_80346AC4 "___", lbl_80346AC8 "NO NAME", lbl_80346AD8 "ENEMIES" (6 sites), lbl_80346AE0 "%d", lbl_80346B58 "%.1f" (2), lbl_80346B7C "TIMER", lbl_80346BF8 "anim" (2), lbl_80346C00 "gen" (2), lbl_80346C04 "critter" (16), lbl_80346C48 "C5" (4), lbl_80346CA0 "A5", lbl_80346CA4 "F2", lbl_80346CA8 "%s%d". The literal is derived by scanning to the first NUL rather than by trusting the declared dimension: `extern char lbl_80346A90[8]` holds a 5-byte string plus 3 bytes of alignment padding, and spelling the padding into the literal is a silent value defect. REVERTED (not committed): the same treatment for lbl_801129D4 "Enemy type %d has bad subtype %d", lbl_801129F8 "No valid worlds", lbl_80112518 "Next Milestone Not Found (%02X)", lbl_80112770 "THERMBASE", lbl_8011277C "THERMCOL" and lbl_80346770 "IT" -- 7 sites. NOT ATTEMPTED, deliberately: lbl_80112370 and lbl_80343BF8 are BLOB BASE POINTERS, not strings. gamemain.c:961 reads `char* fmt = lbl_80112370;` and then calls `FatalErrorf(fmt + 284, ...)`, and gamemain.c:3169 reads `(&lbl_80343BF8[n])[-4]`; both index outside the NUL-terminated string at the symbol, so converting either to a literal is a semantic break that no byte gate would catch as such. A blob-extern string census must screen for offset arithmetic per site -- 2 of the 8 remaining candidates in this TU are of that kind.

attributes.verification: OURS-VS-OURS BYTE PARITY IS THE BAR AND IT IS MET EXACTLY. A scratch A/B (builds build/GUNE5D/src/game/game/.postprocess/body/gamemain.o from HEAD and from the converted source, disassembles both and compares instruction words per function) reports `functions compared: 77 / functions with differing words: 0`. That is a strictly stronger statement than the law's aligned-row procedure: with zero instruction words changed, every new fndiff row is a relocation row by construction. `t16_rederive_body --apply` over all four pins: fn_80054E78, DoWorldAnimation, fn_80051480, fn_800511D0 -- all UNCHANGED, no hash pasted. `wf_ordered_datum_screen.py --unit game/game/gamemain --function <each>`: all four BENIGN, `ordered datum sequences are IDENTICAL - no transposition exists anywhere in the function` -- the move_logic00 datum-swap class this lane was warned about did not occur. `objdump -h` .sdata2 0x58 -> 0xBF (+0x67; the two "%s%d" datums at 0x80346A90 and 0x80346CA8 merge into one entry under -str reuse, which is why the growth is 0x67 and not 0x6C). `defake_gate.py check game/game/gamemain.c --arbiter fuzzy` reports GATE FAILED with two REGRESSION rows -- do_stats_display real 344 -> 350 and fn_80057024 real 218 -> 230 -- and BOTH carry `genuine structural rows FLAT` and a fuzzy delta of exactly +0.0000 (97.5235 -> 97.5235 and 92.7182 -> 92.7182). `fndiff --clean` on both shows every added row as `- R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 <local>` against `+ R_PPC_EMB_SDA21 <local>`, i.e. our pool literal against the target's dtk-named local, which is precisely the flattery the applied law describes. The verdict is overridden on that law's authority and on the zero-word A/B. Three further functions (fn_80054E78, fn_800553B4, fn_80055F68) were classified RELOC-DATUM-EQUAL by the gate itself with the datum values printed and equal. Build: `ninja -j2` -> `build/GUNE5D/main.dol: OK`, retail sha1 7cba77aa496eb0fc5ffec60efd9680aa9635d679. Suites: `python -m unittest discover tools/gdl/tests -b` Ran 2054 tests OK (skipped=2); `python -m memory_graph.test_graph --changed -b` Ran 491 tests OK. PROGRESS SPLIT unmoved at STRICT 57.20% (2594 fns) + EQUIVALENT 11.92% (156 fns), as expected for a keep that changes no byte of the DOL. Baseline re-anchored: `defake_gate.py baseline game/game/gamemain.c --at-head` -> commit ca98f65d3, source sha1 cd172bf15.

hypothesis.statement: The remaining .rodata string ghosts in gamemain (lbl_801129D4, lbl_801129F8, lbl_80112518, lbl_80112770, lbl_8011277C plus the .sdata2 lbl_80346770) are convertible once init_next_level_8005638C's `lis/addi` address form is understood: the function carries `#pragma opt_common_subs off` immediately above it and grows one hoisted `lis rN,0` in its prologue whenever ANYTHING is added to the TU's .rodata, so the lever is that pragma's scope or the address-CSE web it protects, not the strings.
